$f(x) = 4x^2 - 2x^3$, $f'(x) = 8x - 6x^2$, $f''(x) = 8 - 12x$.

For points of inflection, let $f''(x) = 0$:

$$0 = 8 - 12x \implies x = \dfrac{2}{3}$$

When $x = \dfrac{2}{3}$, $f\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{32}{27}$.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & \frac{2}{3}^{-} & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{2}{3}^{+}\\ \hline f''(x) & + & 0 & -\\ \hline\end{array}$$

$\therefore$ as concavity changes at $x = \dfrac{2}{3}$, there is a point of inflection at $\left(\dfrac{2}{3}, \dfrac{32}{27}\right)$.

It is advised to draw a normal distribution graph to illustrate the situation.

595 mL has a $z$-score of $-1$. So $P(595 < X < 600) = 0.34$.

For 602 mL,

$$z = \dfrac{602 - 600}{5} = 0.4$$

In the table, $P(z < 0.4) = 0.655$.

So $P(0 < z < 0.4) = 0.655 - 0.5 = 0.155$.

So $P(600 < X < 602) = 0.155$.

$\therefore P(595 < X < 602) = 0.34 + 0.155 = 0.495$
